bottom_line.text: Bottom line: rs7412 in APOE is best described as: trait-associated common variant without an established monogenic disease role (ClinVar also records a drug-response annotation). Its strongest reported association is with low density lipoprotein cholesterol measurement. Sources disagree on some points (see conflicts). Confidence: high (1155 genome-wide significant associations across 1137 studies).

claims.text: rs7412 is a current dbSNP identifier (not merged into another record).
Earlier identifiers merged into rs7412: rs3200542.
dbSNP records rs7412 as variant type 'snv' on NC_000019.10 (GRCh38) with 1 alternate allele.
Alternate allele 1: NC_000019.10:g.44908822C>T, a single-nucleotide variant (SNV) (C>T in VCF form).
For alternate allele 1 (C>T), Ensembl VEP predicts missense_variant in APOE (ENST00000252486.9:c.526C>T; ENSP00000252486.3:p.Arg176Cys), impact MODERATE.
Ensembl classifies the variant as 'SNV' with allele string C/T.
In gnomAD v2.1.1 exomes, alternate allele 1 (C>T) has an overall allele frequency of 0.0615.

Per-ancestry gnomAD v2.1.1 frequencies for allele 1: African/African American 0.108, Admixed American 0.0312, Ashkenazi Jewish 0.0797, East Asian 0.0742, Finnish 0.0454, Non-Finnish European 0.0751, South Asian 0.0419, Other 0.0608.
In gnomAD v4.1 (exomes and genomes combined), alternate allele 1 (C>T) has an overall allele frequency of 0.0742 (114,390 of 1,540,810 alleles).

Per-ancestry gnomAD v4.1 frequencies for allele 1: African/African American 0.106, Admixed American 0.0349, Ashkenazi Jewish 0.0742, East Asian 0.0605, Finnish 0.0481, Non-Finnish European 0.0783, South Asian 0.0416, Middle Eastern 0.0581, Amish 0.0121, Remaining 0.0705.

ClinVar lists NM_000041.2(APOE):c.526C>T (p.Arg176Cys) (alternate allele 1) with germline classification 'drug response' for: Familial type 3 hyperlipoproteinemia; atorvastatin response - Efficacy; Warfarin response; Hypercholesterolemia; review status 'reviewed by expert panel', 12 submitter(s), allele origin 'germline;unknown'.

Classification history across archived ClinVar releases for this allele: 2018-01: drug response; 2019-01: drug response; 2020-01: drug response; 2026-11: drug response. The classification did not change over these releases.
Individual ClinVar submissions for this allele in the 2026-11 release: 4 'Likely benign', 2 'Benign', 2 'drug response', 1 'Pathogenic', 1 'Uncertain significance', 1 'other', 1 'risk factor'.
Ensembl VEP reports 1 co-located COSMIC somatic mutation record(s) at this position (COSV52986153).
The GWAS Catalog lists 1185 association record(s) for rs7412.
Genome-wide significant association with low density lipoprotein cholesterol measurement (p = 1e-9629, study GCST90239655).
Genome-wide significant association with apolipoprotein B measurement (p = 4e-6067, study GCST90019496, effect allele rs7412-T).
Genome-wide significant association with non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol measurement (p = 1e-4987, study GCST90239667).
Genome-wide significant association with total cholesterol measurement (p = 5e-4551, study GCST90239673).
Genome-wide significant association with cholesteryl esters in large LDL measurement (p = 9e-2168, study GCST90501148, effect allele rs7412-T).
Genome-wide significant association with blood VLDL cholesterol amount (p = 4e-2155, study GCST90501173, effect allele rs7412-T).
LitVar2 links 3605 PubMed articles to rs7412.
Linked article: "Associations Between APOE Polymorphisms, Neurological Symptoms, and Cognitive Assessments in Long COVID Patients: An Analysis of SNPs rs7412 and rs429358" (Mol Neurobiol, 2025).

claims.text: Submitter conflict: ClinVar submissions for NM_000041.2(APOE):c.526C>T (p.Arg176Cys) disagree (1 pathogenic or likely pathogenic, 1 uncertain significance, 6 benign or likely benign); the aggregate classification is 'drug response'.
No allele of rs7412 has a pathogenic or likely pathogenic germline classification in the ClinVar 2026-11 release.

rs7412 is associated with 362 distinct trait(s) at genome-wide significance, and ClinVar holds no pathogenic germline assertion for it, so the evidence supports a trait or risk association and not an established monogenic disease.

Bottom line: rs7412 in APOE is best described as: trait-associated common variant without an established monogenic disease role (ClinVar also records a drug-response annotation). Its strongest reported association is with low density lipoprotein cholesterol measurement. Sources disagree on some points (see conflicts). Confidence: high (1155 genome-wide significant associations across 1137 studies).

Associations Between APOE Polymorphisms, Neurological Symptoms, and Cognitive Assessments in Long COVID Patients: An Analysis of SNPs rs7412 and rs429358.
data.abstract: Long COVID has been associated with persistent neurological symptoms that impair cognitive function and quality of life, raising questions about the role of genetic factors in symptom severity and persistence. Apolipoprotein E (APOE) polymorphisms, known for their relevance in neurodegenerative diseases, may significantly influence neurological outcomes in long COVID patients. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between APOE polymorphisms, specifically single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) rs7412 and rs429358, and neurological and cognitive symptoms in long-term COVID patients. APOE genotypes were identified through the analysis of SNPs rs7412 and rs429358. Cognitive and behavioral assessments were conducted using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), the Pfeffer Functional Activities Questionnaire, the Beck Inventory for mood assessment and the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). Statistical analyses included Mann-Whitney U test, chi-square or Fisher's exact test, and odds ratio calculation, using R Studio and GraphPad Prism. The results indicated that the ε2ε3 genotype was associated with lower scores on the BECK, suggesting fewer depressive symptoms, while the ε3ε3 genotype was linked to an increase in depressive symptoms. Furthermore, analyses of APOE alleles showed an opposite pattern concerning daytime sleepiness: carriers of the ε2 allele exhibited greater daytime sleepiness, whereas ε3 allele carriers reported less sleepiness, as measured by the ESS. The analysis of the rs7412 SNP revealed significant impacts on both BECK and ESS scores. These findings suggest that APOE polymorphisms, particularly the ε2 and ε3 alleles, play a crucial role in modulating neurological and cognitive symptoms associated with long COVID. The results highlight the potential of genetic screening to identify patients at higher risk of persistent cognitive and emotional alterations, emphasizing the importance of personalized management strategies and the need for further research in diverse populations.

data.title: Bioinformatic and genomic analysis identifies C allele of APOE rs7412 as the most prominent variant limiting extreme human longevity.
data.abstract: The genetic factors influencing human longevity have long been a subject of curiosity, linking ancient historical records with modern genomic research. This study seeks to identify key genetic contributors to lifespan by integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with functional annotations across multiple biological databases. Among our findings, APOE emerged as one of the most prominent gene, with the rs7412-C variant showing a strong association with reduced lifespan due to its widely distributed across global populations. Additionally, we observed that rs449647-A and rs405509-T were more frequently found in regions with longer life expectancies, such as Asia, and were less common in African populations, suggesting a possible genetic influence on regional lifespan variations. These findings provide a basis for future research into the genetic mechanisms underlying aging and may contribute to the development of strategies to promote healthy aging.

data.title: Common Variants rs429358 and rs7412 in APOE Gene Are Not Associated with POAG in a Saudi Cohort.
data.abstract: Adult-onset glaucoma, an age-related neurodegenerative disease, is very prevalent among the elderly Arabs of Saudi origin. This study investigated the association between apolipoprotein E (APOE) gene variants (rs429358 and rs7412) and primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) in Arabs of Saudi origin. A case-control genetic association study involving 179 POAG patients and 251 controls utilized Sanger sequencing to genotype APOE gene variants. The allele frequencies and genotype distributions for rs429358 and rs7412 did not show significant associations with POAG. The haplotype analysis revealed apoε3 (87.6% and 87.4%) as the most prevalent, followed by ε4 (2.8% and 3.6%) and ε2 (9.6% and 8.9%) in the controls and POAG patients, respectively. Although the ε2/ε3 genotype and ε2-carriers displayed a more than two-fold increased risk, statistical significance was not reached. Notably, these polymorphisms did not affect clinical markers, such as intraocular pressure and cup/disc ratio. The logistic regression analysis demonstrated no significant influence of age, sex, rs429358, or rs7412 polymorphisms on POAG. In conclusion, within the Saudi cohort, APOE variants (rs429358 and rs7412) do not appear to be associated with POAG and are not substantial risk factors for its development. However, additional population-based studies are required to validate these findings.
